title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: An external magnetic field can modulate rare-earth luminescence and circular polarization when the complex has strong anisotropy or a chiral lattice, contrary to the assumption that 4f emission is magnetically insensitive.
explanation: Assembly of chiral (R/S)-1-(3-bromophenyl)ethylammonium with EuCl3− is reported to show room-temperature magneto-photoluminescence: the field splits excited levels and promotes dark excitons into emissive states. Strongly anisotropic bidentate Dy(III) complexes use field-induced moment polarization to disturb the electron cloud and direct circularly polarized light.
scope: Chiral Eu(III) hybrids and magnetically anisotropic Dy(III) complexes.
conditions: Applied magnetic field; chiral organic cation for the Eu MPL example; bidentate coordination that enforces Dy anisotropy.
caveats: The Eu MPL observation is a first room-temperature report in this review and lacks a reference number in the Markdown. Field strengths are not given.
